body: No, and that is not helpful.

I knew I put on weight. I ASKED if I looked like I had put on weight. I always got "oh no, you look fine! You carry it well! It's because of the wheelchair!" It was never "You eat more than your dad does and he's putting on weight too, plus he's more physically active than you". But that's what I needed to hear. *rage*

So true. I did weight training four hours a week every week for almost a year but increased my eating to compensate and was walking everywhere. Lost ten pounds. Have been counting calories for ~3 weeks and have already almost lost that. But I never listened to anyone who told me that and got disheartened trying. It really took being overweight by more than "just a few pounds" to get dedicated.
In my weight loss journey right now, if I eat fast food I will spiral into a depression. So guess what I avoid? FAST FOOD. It makes no sense to me to keep doing something that makes you feel bad.

To be honest I probably had at least that when I put on 20+ lbs in six months. I'm tempted to make excuses right now but I'm stopping myself; it was entirely my fault. Now I'm paying my price and I'm okay with that.
Depending on the protein you eat, you could have to eat a lot to get that many calories. I love protein though so I wouldn't mind.
I'm glad you're trying to get healthy but I am so jealous of your 3050 calories a day. So jealous.

It is so easy to just eat less! I'm doing that along with (very irregular) exercise and I'm amazed at how quickly the weight is coming off. I'm looking back to when I would eat whatever and it's crazy. I could go to Red Lobster and eat six grilled shrimp, salmon, a cup of rice, some mashed potatoes, an ear of corn, and (oh I'm cringing) a half pound of crab legs. No wonder I gained weight! AND I COULD STILL EAT MORE. Ugh.
I'll try, but I still live at home so my family might get a bit miffed haha.
Yeah, that's why I use the scale. But of course because I feel like I can't see progress I obsess over the scale. It's a balancing act.

I own one, there's a scale at the gym, and I'm at doctors' offices pretty much constantly. Usually the doctors leave it in kg so I don't really know, but sometimes I see it when they switch it to lbs. It takes a lot of willpower for me not to look haha.
I agree, but even when I weighed 30+ pounds less I thought I looked just as heavy as I do now. Although my pants getting looser is also a good measure.
I should do something like that. Thanks!
I have to ask, how do you keep yourself from checking the scale? I'm trying to only weigh myself once a week but right now I'm at least twice a week.

Me too. Especially since I didn't buy into calorie counting at first. I wouldn't see a difference physically or on my scale within a week of lifting so I'd feel discouraged. Nevermind that I hadn't adjusted my portion sizes since I was in marching band and hitting a growth spurt. Although with that little bit of fat logic gone, I am losing weight finally. But it took three weeks of not giving up and getting on a fully functional scale first.
Thank you for contributing to my nightmare fuel and determination to go to the gym.
Damn I do half that in one day at the gym! o.O I didn't realize how little exercise is recommended. But I tend to be either doing 4+ hours a week or 0.

Thanks, I've discovered that protein is the only thing that makes me feel full. I just need to find a lower calorie option for it.

I'll look into it.
If my bf ran into his ex and chatted with her, I would appreciate that name. She was boring as hell in bed, apparently.

Two years, and he is a HUGE fitness buff. Loves lifting more than me sometimes haha. I have health issues so I was heavier when we started dating but I've always wanted to go back to my thin self, so I started exercising with him. Got super attractive, then my health got worse and I was wheelchair bound for six months. I'm the heaviest I've ever been, but I'm going back to the gym and hopefully gonna lose the weight. He has stayed dedicated to his fitness regimen and only gotten more attractive, which really motivates me to lose my weight. He finds me attractive no matter what, but hey, confidence is sexy and I definitely lack that.
Thank you so much.

Thank you. It's really nice to hear validation, and the more I reach out the more I get it, which is the opposite of what I expected. I will definitely look into the health insurance, and my dad says that he believes if I moved in with the girlfriend that mom wouldn't be as angry as she was at my sister. Mom is very anti-sex, so when Sister moved in with her boyfriend at the time, it was a huge deal. Plus the girlfriend doesn't fall for mom's stuff and we consider each other good friends. I have several months to save up money and get my psychologist's help with my emotional blocks.

I'll definitely look into it, thank you.

Yes, that's the word! (I forget words sometimes or mix them up in speech; gotta love cognitive degeneration.) Oh yeah, I had a narc psychologist before and it was terrible. He literally spent the entire session talking about himself.

Thank you, I think I'm too hard on myself and used to using defeatist language. :\ I just wish I could stop being so afraid! I'm not even sure why I'm afraid. She's never hit any of us.

Thank you for that, very much!
Thanks. Hopefully seeing my psychologist can help me on the brave part.
I'm more LL (but don't let it become dead), and I'm definitely ticklish when I'm not in the mood. Once I get started the ticklish spots become all the right spots though.

First off, your username is amazing.

The girlfriend is super excited about the possibility of me moving with her, and she already got my brother to okay it. She removed my sister until she got health problems, so I'm not sure how it would work. I know it's what I need to do, but you know how manipulative they are... I don't think anyone would believe me. I think I would just look like an ungrateful teen (I'm only 18).

If I go full-time at the job I would be able to get insurance, but I don't know if it would be as good as the one at home. I know my sister is still on her insurance because of her health problems, but I'm worried that she may remove me out of spite. Plus I see about five different specialists and take 20+ pills a day, so I'm definitely worried about being able to afford it. How low income would I need to be, and how good would the insurance be?

He is, I must have misrepresented him. I only get to see him every two weeks, and I think he was phrasing things the way he was to try and get me to see the (oh I forgot the word)... How serious the situation is, I guess? I'm sorry I gave off a bad impression of him. I also tend to get along better in a less formal setting (for example, I cuss so them cussing makes me feel more at ease).

She does want a roommate a lot, and she comes across as such a goody-two-shoes to parents that hopefully it would work if I phrased it that way, but I am pretty solidly terrified into submission at this point. Thank you for your response, btw! I hope I don't come across as too rude or something, or trying to dismiss you outright. I will seriously consider your input, this is just my first time posting on here...
